name: Cross-tradition comparisons

concepts.title: Resist methods: clay pastes, lime outlines and wax
concepts.summary: Ajrakh gach is a paste of tree gum, clay (lal mitti), water and millet flour, with alum added to half of it; the clay and millet resist indigo while the alum acts as mordant.
concepts.body_md:
Ajrakh gach is a paste of tree gum, clay (lal mitti), water and millet flour, with alum added to half of it; the clay and millet resist indigo while the alum acts as mordant. [ajrakh:S1]

Ajrakh white outlines (khariyanu) are printed with a lime and tree-gum resist. [ajrakh:S1]

Dabu paste is mud, gum and lime; the Deesa paste uses river-bed silt. [dabu:S1, dabu:S3]

In Dabu sources lime is the weakest resist, used for fine outlines, mud is used for repeated indigo immersion and sand for absorbent colours. [dabu:S6]

Bagru and Sanganeri dabu paste mixes black clay (kali mitti), lime, wheat flour and gum in ratios that depend on the type of dabu needed, and is used only for indigo patterns. [bagru:S1, sanganeri:S1]

Beeswax is listed as a Machilipatnam raw material; wax applied with a kalam before indigo appears in a general kalamkari description. [machilipatnam-kalamkari:S4, machilipatnam-kalamkari:S5]
